correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary existing simple Steiner 2-(v,k,1), N N^T=(r−1)I+J and r(k−1)+1=v. The displayed potentials x=(k/v)e_p−(1/v)1_B, y=(N^T x−e_B)/k solve the unit source Poisson equation and give the unique cut projection current. Each edge-avoiding path has length at least 5; selecting the first second-block neighbor x outside B and z in B\{p} yields exactly (v−k)(k−1) paths; their 1/(kv) signed contributions match every nonzero current-table entry. Their total weight is 1−ρ, ρ=(k−1)/v+1/k, without cancellation; ||Q||_1=||Q||_∞=5−4ρ, ||I−Q||=6(1−ρ). Rank N=v implies b>=v and excludes k>=4 dominance; admissible k=3 small orders are 7 and 9. Independent Fano-projective-plane grounded-Laplacian pseudoinverse confirms all columns (~2.52380952 and ~2.28571429) and idempotence; finite examples corroborate rather than prove the universal statement.
residual_risks: The exact current law assumes unit conductances and λ=1; no assertion for arbitrary optimal projections or intermediate p.
